review.translation: [Then|0] [the flood|1] [on|4] [the earth|5] [lasted|0] [forty|2] [days|3], [and|6] [the waters|7] [increased|6] [and lifted|8] [the ark|10,9] [so that it rose|11] [off|12] [the ground|13].

analysis.evidence: אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם, “forty days,” specifies how long הַמַּבּוּל, “the flood,” was on the earth. The duration phrase gives הָיָה its contextual sense “lasted.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed narrative conjunction וַ־. The verb agrees with הַמַּבּוּל, “the flood.”
analysis.sense: to continue for a period of time

draft.change: Define the flood itself, add Genesis 7:17 as defining evidence, and retain Psalm 29:10 as an example.
draft.definition: An inundation in which waters overwhelm the land.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 7:17 the rising waters lift the ark from the ground.

analysis.evidence: The flood lasts forty days עַל הָאָרֶץ, “upon the earth.” The next clause describes its effect: the waters increase and lift the ark above the ground.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־, with doubling of the initial מ, prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: An inundation of the land by water.

analysis.evidence: In אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם, אַרְבָּעִים gives the number forty and יוֹם supplies the unit of time. The flood lasted forty days.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, common gender, plural absolute, with no prefix or pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם, “forty days,” the numeral אַרְבָּעִים counts days to express the duration of the flood. Hebrew uses the singular noun יוֹם here.
עַל הָאָרֶץ means “on the earth” and tells where the flood lasted forty days.
In וַיְהִי הַמַּבּוּל אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם עַל הָאָרֶץ, the phrase עַל הָאָרֶץ identifies the earth as the place where the flood lasted forty days.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, common gender, singular absolute, with prefixed definite article הָ־.

analysis.evidence: The plural verb agrees with its subject הַמַּיִם, “the waters.” The next clause says that the waters lifted the ark, showing that the floodwater increased in volume.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural, with prefixed conjunction וַ־.

draft.change: Extend the existing floodwater citation to begin at Genesis 7:17 and identify the action that establishes the sense.
draft.definition: מַיִם denotes a body or flow of water, here the floodwaters that lift the ark.
draft.evidence: Genesis 7:17 identifies the waters by their action: they increase and lift the ark above the ground.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 7:17, הַמַּיִם is the subject of וַיִּרְבּוּ, “they increased,” and remains the subject of וַיִּשְׂאוּ אֶת הַתֵּבָה, “they lifted the ark.” The waters of the flood increased until they lifted the ark above the ground.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural noun in the absolute state, with the prefixed definite article הַ־ and consequent doubling of מ.
analysis.sense: a body or flow of water

analysis.evidence: הַמַּיִם (the waters) is the plural subject, and אֶת־הַתֵּבָה marks the ark as the direct object. The next clause, וַתָּרָם מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ (and it rose above the ground), confirms that the waters lifted the ark.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural, with prefixed וַ־.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּשְׂאוּ אֶת הַתֵּבָה, “they lifted the ark,” the subject is הַמַּיִם, “the waters.” אֶת marks הַתֵּבָה, “the ark,” as the definite direct object of וַיִּשְׂאוּ.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add the feminine noun תֵּבָה under its own consonants תבה. The supplied gentilic gloss and root תאר do not fit the object lifted by the waters.
draft.definition: A watertight container that holds people or animals on the water. In Genesis 7:17 it is Noah’s ark.
draft.evidence: Genesis 6:14 describes the ark’s timber construction and pitch coating. Genesis 7:17 shows the floodwaters lifting it.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks הַתֵּבָה as the object of וַיִּשְׂאוּ. The rising waters lifted the ark. The feminine singular וַתָּרָם then agrees with תֵּבָה and describes the ark rising above the ground.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun.
analysis.sense: The ark that carried Noah, his household, and the animals through the flood.

analysis.evidence: The waters lift הַתֵּבָה, “the ark.” The ark then becomes the subject of the feminine singular וַתָּרָם, and מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ describes its movement up from the ground.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person feminine singular, with prefixed conjunction וַ־.

analysis.evidence: The waters lift the ark, and וַתָּרָם מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ means “it rose off the ground.” עַל marks the ground as the supporting surface, and מֵ־ marks movement away from it.
analysis.morphology: Preposition עַל with prefixed מֵ־ (מִן, “from”), governing הָאָרֶץ.

analysis.evidence: The waters lift the ark, and וַתָּרָם מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ says that it rose above the ground. The ground is the surface from which the ark was lifted.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a common noun, singular absolute, of common gender.
